data.title: Correction to 3M Stock Rises on Upgrade. Why This Analyst Likes Its Transformation. — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Al Root

3M stock rose Friday after catching an upgrade. It isn't an upgrade to Buy, though.

Bernstein analyst Varun Govindaraj upgraded shares to the equivalent of Hold from Sell. His price target went to $171 from $145.

3M stock rose 1.8% in midday trading to $170.45, while the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average were up 0.5% and 0.8%, respectively.

"We are upgrading 3M to Market Perform based on a refreshed understanding of the transformation," wrote Govindaraj. "Four factors drive our decision," including an improving economy, margin expansion opportunity, improved R&D spending, and reduced risk tied to 3M's manufacturing of so-called PFAS forever chemicals.

An improving economy is a tailwind for any business. The Institute for Supply Management Purchasing Managers' Index, or ISM PMI, has been above 50, a level that indicates growth, for several months after several years below that level.

Internally, things are improving, too.

CEO Bill Brown took over in May 2024 and has focused on operational efficiency and product innovation. Some green shoots of improvement are emerging.

Comparable sales growth is expected to be 3.5% in 2026, up from 1.5% in 2025 and 1.2% in 2024. As for profit margins, they have increased a couple of percentage points over the past two years. Analysts expect a couple more points of improvement over the next two years.

PFAS liabilities have been an overhang for years, but a roughly $12.5 billion settlement in 2023 gave investors some certainty over the size of potential payments.

Coming into Friday's trading, 3M stock was up about 5% year to date and up 9% over the past 12 months. Shares haven't done much lately, but since Brown took over 3M stock has gained about 70%, 17 percentage points better than the S&P 500.

Overall, Wall Street remains a little skeptical. Only 43% of analysts covering 3M stock rate shares Buy. The average Buy-rating ratio for S&P 500 stocks typically ranges from 55% to 60%.

At least there is one fewer call to sell the stock.

data.title: Discipline, Data & Digital Finance: Celebrating Vikas Khandelwal
data.description:
On his birthday, we celebrate Vikas Khandelwal, CFO at Reliance Retail, whose 25-year career spans finance, corporate planning and strategy across leading Indian companies

On his birthday today, we celebrate Vikas Khandelwal, Chief Financial Officer at Reliance Retail, one of India’s largest and most diversified retail conglomerates. With a career spanning 25 years, Khandelwal has built a reputation as a performance-driven finance leader with deep expertise across financial planning and analysis (FP&A), budgeting, forecasting, business partnering and strategic finance.

A Chartered Accountant from the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India and a Bachelor of Commerce graduate from the University of Rajasthan, Khandelwal’s journey has taken him across some of the most recognised names in Indian industry — Ambuja Cements, Tata Chemicals and LG Electronics India — before he joined Reliance Retail in 2022. Along the way, he has worked across cement, chemicals, consumer electronics, and consumer durables and appliances, gaining cross-sector exposure in plant accounting, management accounting, corporate planning and financial strategy.

Khandelwal’s career is marked by a steady progression through senior finance roles — from Senior Officer, Accounts at Ambuja Cements, to Team Lead, Management Accounting and Subsidy at Tata Chemicals, to nearly 14 years at LG Electronics India as Head of Corporate Planning, where he partnered closely with CXOs to drive strategic planning, profitability and performance analytics for the India business. At Reliance Retail, he has moved from Vice President, Financial Planning and Strategy to his current mandate as CFO (Own Brands), leading financial strategy for a multi-brand consumer durables and appliances business with a nationwide distribution footprint.

Across these roles, he has focused on working capital and cash flow management, cost optimisation, supply chain finance, pricing strategy, return on investment (ROI) analysis, capital expenditure (capex) evaluation and building key performance indicator (KPI)-led governance frameworks — with an emphasis on digital finance transformation and automated reporting.

Khandelwal has continued to invest in new-age capabilities alongside his core finance expertise, recently completing certifications including ‘Generative AI for Leaders’ from Vanderbilt University and ‘Finance of Mergers and Acquisitions: Valuation and Pricing’ from the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign.

As he celebrates his birthday, BW CFO World extends warm wishes to Vikas Khandelwal for a year of continued growth, impact and leadership

data.title: Runwal Enterprises Rs 500 Crore IPO Opens Today
data.description:
Ahead of the issue, Runwal Enterprises raises Rs 148.9 crore from anchor investors

Runwal Enterprises, a Mumbai-based real estate developer, will open its Rs 500 crore initial public offering (IPO) for subscription on 25 September, with the company looking to tap investor demand amid continued growth in its residential sales.

The IPO will remain open until 29 September and has a price band of Rs 290-305 per share. At the upper end of the band, the company will raise Rs 500 crore. Investors can bid for a minimum of 49 shares and in multiples thereafter.

Ahead of the issue, Runwal Enterprises raised Rs 148.9 crore from anchor investors. The company allotted 48.83 lakh shares to nine institutional investors at Rs 305 apiece, the upper end of the price band.

Tata Mutual Fund was the largest participant in the anchor book, acquiring 13.11 lakh shares for Rs 40 crore. Maybank Securities picked up 8.19 lakh shares for Rs 25 crore, while Authum Investment and Infrastructure was allotted 6.44 lakh shares worth Rs 19.6 crore.

Runwal Enterprises recorded consolidated sales value of Rs 2,353.5 crore in financial year 2026, up 24 per cent from Rs 1,899 crore in FY25.

The company’s total saleable area also expanded to 2.07 million square feet in FY26 from 1.62 million square feet a year earlier.

However, average selling price moderated to Rs 11,366 per square foot in FY26 from Rs 11,754 per square foot in the previous year. The increase in sales value was therefore accompanied by a significant expansion in saleable area, even as average realisations declined.

Runwal Enterprises plans to use Rs 100 crore from the fresh issue to repay or prepay borrowings at the company. Another Rs 225 crore will be invested in its wholly owned material subsidiaries, Runwal Residency and Evie Real Estate, to repay a portion of their outstanding debt.

As of July 2026, Runwal Enterprises had standalone borrowings of Rs 431.4 crore. Runwal Residency and Evie Real Estate had outstanding borrowings of Rs 286.5 crore and Rs 356.4 crore, respectively.

The remaining proceeds will be used to fund acquisitions of future real estate projects and for general corporate purposes.

The company has positioned the IPO as a means to support its project pipeline while strengthening its balance sheet as it expands its residential development business.

ICICI Securities and Jefferies India are the merchant bankers managing the Runwal Enterprises IPO.

data.title: Orient Cables IPO Opens On 25 Sept; Raises Rs 165.6 Cr From Anchor Investors
data.description:
Orient Cables (India), a Gurugram-based manufacturer of networking and specialty cables, opened for public subscription on 25 September for its Rs 552 crore initial public offering (IPO).

The company also raised Rs 165.6 crore from anchor investors alloting 60.88 lakh shares to 14 anchor investors at Rs 272 apiece, the upper end of its Rs 258-272 price band. The IPO will remain open until 29 September.

Domestic mutual funds accounted for the bulk of the anchor allocation, with eight fund houses receiving 41.17 lakh shares. The list includes Nippon Life India, ICICI Prudential Asset Management Company, Aditya Birla Sun Life Asset Management Company, Motilal Oswal Asset Management Company, Invesco, Bandhan Mutual Fund, Sundaram Mutual Fund and Edelweiss.

Insurance companies also participated, with Aditya Birla Sun Life Insurance and Edelweiss Life Insurance together acquiring 4.26 lakh shares worth Rs 11.58 crore. Other institutional investors in the anchor book included Goldman Sachs, Ashoka WhiteOak, 360 ONE WAM and Border to Coast Pensions Partnership.

Orient Cables plans to raise Rs 552 crore through the IPO, comprising a fresh issue of Rs 320 crore and an offer for sale (OFS) of up to Rs 232 crore by the promoter Nagpal family.

The company plans to deploy Rs 91.5 crore from the fresh issue towards machinery and equipment purchases and civil works at its manufacturing facilities. A further Rs 155.5 crore will be used to repay or prepay debt, with the balance earmarked for general corporate purposes.

As of June 2026, Orient Cables had total outstanding borrowings of Rs 258.4 crore, including Rs 240.4 crore of secured fund-based facilities.

The planned debt reduction will therefore account for a significant portion of the fresh capital raised, while the proposed investment in machinery and manufacturing infrastructure is aimed at expanding its production capabilities.

In the grey market, Orient Cables shares were commanding a premium of around 42 per cent over the upper end of the IPO price band on 25 September. However, grey market premiums are unofficial and can change materially before listing.

Orient Cables manufactures networking cables, specialty power cables, optical fibre cables and wire and cable harness assemblies, catering to the broader connectivity and electrical infrastructure ecosystem.

IIFL Capital Services and JM Financial are the merchant bankers managing the IPO.

data.title: India’s Growth Story Broadens Beyond AI, Says Jefferies
data.description:
The latest GREED & fear report points to rising private capex, electrification, advanced manufacturing and energy demand as key structural themes for India

India’s structural growth story could remain resilient even as investor focus on artificial intelligence and related infrastructure evolves, according to Jefferies’ latest GREED & fear report, titled The Virtues Of Small Over Large.

The report argues that while the global AI investment cycle is generating significant spending on data centres and computing infrastructure, India’s growth drivers extend well beyond the technology theme. Private sector capital expenditure, electrification, renewable energy, advanced manufacturing and rising electricity demand are emerging as important areas of focus.

AI Investment Faces Questions Over Capacity

The report raises questions about the scale of capital expenditure planned by major US hyperscalers as AI infrastructure investment accelerates.

Jefferies notes that consensus estimates currently point to around USD 990 billion of capex by four major hyperscalers in 2027. The report questions whether such a level of spending will ultimately be required, particularly as companies explore more efficient ways of deploying AI computing capacity.

The report also cites research indicating that Anthropic server utilisation had declined 26 per cent from its January 2026 peak, while cautioning that the finding comes from third-party research and should be interpreted accordingly.

Another theme highlighted is the development of small language models (SLMs). Citing a Stanford University study, Jefferies notes that SLMs are narrowing the performance gap with large language models while requiring substantially lower energy and computing costs.

The report suggests this could encourage greater use of on-premises AI systems by companies, potentially reducing dependence on centralised cloud infrastructure for certain applications.

India’s Structural Growth Drivers

Against this backdrop, Jefferies points to several areas supporting India’s longer-term growth. A separate Jefferies report on India’s “new industrial revolution” identified six areas combining policy support and rising private sector participation: space, semiconductors, solar manufacturing, data centres, electronics and aerospace.

The report notes that government support for these sectors is visible through measures including incentive schemes, tax holidays and localisation requirements.

The growth of global capability centres is another indicator cited in the report. India added 111 greenfield GCCs in the first eight months of 2026, according to data referenced by Jefferies, with these centres expected to create around 70,000-75,000 jobs.

Office demand has also strengthened, with net absorption rising from 21 million sq ft in 2021 to 61 million sq ft in 2025 and an estimated 60 million sq ft in 2026.

Electrification Emerges As A Key Theme

Energy and electrification are highlighted as another major structural opportunity for India.

Jefferies points to the expansion of renewable energy, particularly solar power, and the development of battery storage as important components of the country’s future electricity infrastructure.

The report draws comparisons with China, where the expansion of the electricity grid and improvements in battery storage have helped bring down the cost of solar power. It suggests that similar developments in India could support the country’s manufacturing ambitions by reducing the cost of electricity over time.

The report also cites projections from Hitachi Energy India that total final energy demand could increase by 50 per cent and electricity demand by 100 per cent by 2035, reaching 3,365 TWh.

As a result, electricity’s share of total final energy demand is projected to rise from 19 per cent in 2023 to 25 per cent in 2035, supported by growth in renewables, energy storage and smart demand management.

Private Capex Shows Signs Of Recovery

The report also highlights signs of a long-awaited recovery in private sector capital expenditure in India.

India’s annualised nominal gross fixed capital formation-to-GDP ratio increased from a recent low of 31.4 per cent in the four quarters to December to 32.4 per cent in the four quarters to June.

At the same time, machinery imports have increased substantially, rising from USD 29 billion in FY21 to USD 62 billion in FY26 and USD 66 billion in the 12 months to August 2026.

Jefferies also notes that India is already a major global producer across several traditional manufacturing categories, including crude steel, cement, ammonia, mobile phones and solar modules, although production remains significantly below China’s levels in several of these industries.

The report therefore places India’s manufacturing opportunity within a broader combination of domestic demand, policy support, private investment and infrastructure development.

India’s Growth Story Beyond The AI Cycle

The report’s broader message is that India’s structural growth drivers are not dependent solely on the global AI investment cycle.

While AI remains a major technology and investment theme, Jefferies highlights electrification, renewable energy, manufacturing, private capex and infrastructure as areas that could continue to shape India’s economic trajectory.

The report also makes clear that its views represent Jefferies’ research assessment and that the investment themes discussed carry risks and uncertainties. It does not constitute personalised investment advice.

data.title: AceVector IPO Opens On 25 Sept; Price Band Fixed At Rs 32
data.description:
AceVector, the parent company of Snapdeal and Unicommerce eSolutions, is set for public subscription on September 25 and close on September 29 with the price band fixed the price band at Rs 30-32 per equity share.

The Kunal Bahl and Rohit Kumar Bansal-promoted company, which counts SoftBank among its investors, is targeting a total issue size of Rs 420 crore at the upper end of the price band.

The IPO comprises a fresh issue of shares worth up to Rs 287 crore and an offer for sale (OFS) of Rs 133 crore. The shares have a face value of Rs 1 each.

Existing investors, including SoftBank subsidiary Starfish and Nexus Venture Partners, will participate in the OFS. Other selling shareholders include FIH Business Global, Kenneth Stuart Glass, Jason Ashok Kothari, Rupen Investment and Industries, Centaurus Trading and Investments, and Laurent Bernard Amouyal.

Starfish is currently AceVector’s largest shareholder with a 30.11 per cent stake. Bahl holds 12.19 per cent, while Bansal owns 10.93 per cent. B2 Professional Services LLP, owned by the wives of Bahl and Bansal, holds another 10.87 per cent.

How AceVector Plans To Use IPO Proceeds

Of the total issue, 75 per cent has been reserved for qualified institutional buyers (QIBs), while non-institutional investors (NIIs) will be allocated 15 per cent. The remaining 10 per cent will be reserved for retail investors.

The company plans to deploy Rs 132 crore from the net proceeds of the fresh issue towards marketing and business promotion for its marketplace business. Another Rs 50 crore has been earmarked for technology infrastructure for the marketplace business.

The remaining proceeds will be used for inorganic growth, including acquisitions, and general corporate purposes.

Revenue Growth, Losses Narrow

Gurugram-headquartered AceVector operates an asset-light digital commerce ecosystem comprising value-focused e-commerce marketplace Snapdeal, e-commerce enablement software-as-a-service (SaaS) platform Unicommerce eSolutions and consumer brands housed under Stellaro Brands.

The company continues to report losses, although its deficit narrowed in financial year 2026. Net loss stood at Rs 60.7 crore in FY26, compared with Rs 139.2 crore in the previous financial year.

Revenue from operations, meanwhile, increased 29.2 per cent to Rs 510.4 crore in FY26 from Rs 395 crore a year earlier.

IIFL Capital Services, CLSA India and Systematix Corporate Services have been appointed as the merchant bankers to the issue.

data.title: Sunteck Realty receives ₹59 crore GST notice for TDR procurement in FY23
data.description:
Real estate firm Sunteck Realty Ltd on Friday (September 25) disclosed that it has received a show-cause notice (SCN) from the Department of Goods and Services Tax for FY23, involving a demand of ₹59.44 crore, including interest and penalty.

"Sunteck Realty Limited (“the company”) has received a SCN under section 73 of the GST Act from the Department of Goods and Services Tax for the Financial Year 2022-23 for tax liability on procurement of Transferable Development Rights (TDR) from the open market, which was originally granted by Local Bodies, aggregating to ₹59,43,79,402/- (including the amount of interest and penalty)," according to a stock exchange filing.

The notice relates to the company’s procurement of Transferable Development Rights (TDR) from the open market, which were originally granted by local bodies.

Sunteck Realty said the notice was issued under Section 73 of the GST Act. The company said it believes no GST is applicable to such transactions as they do not constitute a supply of goods or services and are therefore outside the scope of GST.

The company said it will file a reply before the Office of the Deputy Commissioner of State Tax, Mazgaon, Mumbai, disputing the demand.

Sunteck also said the notice has considered an amount that is twice the actual amount. It added that the notice was issued despite a detailed, comprehensive audit for the financial year already having been concluded by the tax authorities.

The company said there is no impact on its financial, operational or other activities arising from the show-cause notice. Sunteck said it was studying the notice and evaluating its compliance obligations. It added that it will take all necessary action to present and defend its case before the adjudicating authorities.

Shares of Sunteck Realty Ltd ended at ₹282.25, down by ₹1.90, or 0.67%, on the BSE.

data.title: Why Meta Stock Could Spike if It Crosses This Price Target — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Kit Norton

Shares of Meta Platforms are having a moment, fueled by excitement from Wall Street and consumers alike around the Facebook-parent's consumer artificial-intelligence model Muse and the company's overarching AI ecosystem.

The stock's recent surge could just be the beginning if it's able to claim a key price level.

Meta stock declined 2.9% to $754.88 on Friday after ending Thursday up 4.5%. Even as shares fell Friday, the stock has risen more than 13% this week and was on pace for its best monthly gain in more than 13 years, according to Dow Jones Market Data.

Muse ignited the rally, with both the company and analysts claiming it may be the biggest AI release since OpenAI's ChatGPT stormed onto the scene. Meta followed up the release with its Connect keynote presentation and Wall Street has been busily raising price targets on the stock as upside seems much more attainable.

While Meta has risen solidly this month, the stock price has remained stubbornly below $800. Shares on Friday were 4.4% below their record closing high of $790 from Aug. 12, 2025.

The stock has also been range-bound for more than a year, trading around the $600 level and to the high $790s, according to chart analysis. If shares are able to break out of that range and claim the $800 price level, the recent Muse rally might just be the beginning.

Wall Street's recent price target hikes are constructive of this view.

Canaccord Genuity analyst Maria Ripps raised her price target on Meta to $950 from $930, which represents 22% upside from the closing price of $777.59 on Thursday. Ripps also maintained her Buy rating on Meta stock.

"We expect the shares to keep re-rating higher as Muse demonstrates that Meta's model and infrastructure spending can support a product that earns from subscriptions and, over time, transaction fees, with advertising as additional optionality," Ripps said in a research note.

The analyst added that Meta's reach across its apps, together with an advertising business that can fund a free agent for years, "gives it room to keep Muse's fees low while stand-alone AI developers may face pressure to monetize their agents sooner."

Ripps wasn't alone in this view. TD Cowen analyst John Blackledge on Friday hiked his Meta stock price target to $865 from $750.

Blackledge said in the research note that Meta's AI ecosystem has crystalized with the release of Muse.

"We are encouraged by the plethora of hardware that will support Muse AI, as well as by the release timeline," the analyst noted, referring to the company updates from Meta's Connect event.

But Muse was at the heart of the bullish view. Blackledge estimated that global revenue from Muse could rise from $55 million in 2026 to $1.8 billion in 2027 and hit $27 billion in 2030. That would represent about 6% of Meta's total revenue, according to Blackledge.

Deutsche Bank analyst Benjamin Black also believes that Meta stock can claim the $800 price level and move even higher on the Muse boost. The analyst on Friday raised his price target to $820 from $750.

Black said in the research note that Meta seems to be primarily focused on building a strong user base for Muse that it could monetize in the future and that the Facebook parent may eventually offer subscription tiers based on data usage.

Some of Wall Street's recent Meta price target hikes were even larger.

Tigress Financial Partners analyst Ivan Feinseth sees 28% upside for Meta stock. He raised his price target to $995 from $945 on the potential of Muse to change Meta's role for the consumer.

"If users make it part of their routines, META gains opportunities in subscriptions and commerce alongside advertising. The financial scale of those opportunities has yet to be established, but the product represents a meaningful expansion of what META can offer its global network," Feinseth said in the research note.

data.title: Annamycin Turns “Cold” Pancreatic Tumors “Hot” in New Preclinical Data Presented at AACR
data.description:
Data presented at the AACR Conference on Pancreatic Cancer indicate Annamycin’s antitumor activity is partially mediated by CD8+ T cells, supporting a potential immune-mediated mechanism alongside its direct cytotoxic activity

HOUSTON, Sept. 25, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Moleculin Biotech, Inc. (“Moleculin” or the “Company”) today announced new preclinical data indicating that the antitumor activity of its lead drug candidate, Annamycin (naxtarubicin), in pancreatic cancer is partially mediated by CD8+ T cell cytotoxicity. The findings are being presented at the AACR Conference on Pancreatic Cancer: New Frontiers in Biology and Therapeutic Development, held September 25–28, 2026 in San Diego, California.

In preclinical models of pancreatic cancer, Annamycin’s antitumor activity appears to depend in part on CD8+ T cells, the immune system’s primary tumor-killing cells. The finding suggests Annamycin may do more than kill cancer cells directly; it may also expose tumors that are typically considered immunologically “cold” to immune attack.

Pancreatic cancer is among the most treatment-resistant solid tumors, and its characteristically “cold” immune microenvironment is one reason checkpoint inhibitors have shown limited single-agent activity in the disease. Preclinical evidence that Annamycin’s activity is partly immune-mediated points to a potential basis for combination approaches, and complements the immune-modulating mechanism of the Company’s WP1066 program.

Title: “Turning cold pancreatic tumors hot: Antitumor activity of Annamycin is partially mediated by CD8+ T cell cytotoxicity”

Author/Presenter: Angela T. Alistar, MD, Morristown Medical Center, Atlantic Health System / Carol G. Simon Cancer Center

Congress: AACR Conference on Pancreatic Cancer: New Frontiers in Biology and Therapeutic Development

Dates: September 25–28, 2026

Location: Hilton San Diego Bayfront, San Diego, California

These findings were generated in preclinical models. Preclinical results may not be predictive of results in humans, and Annamycin is not currently in clinical development for the treatment of pancreatic cancer.

The abstract for this presentation was published today as a supplement to the September 15, 2026 issue of Cancer Research.

“Annamycin represents a fundamental re-engineering of the anthracycline, one designed to increase efficacy and avoid multidrug resistance and the cardiotoxicity of currently prescribed agents,” said Walter Klemp, Chairman, President and Chief Executive Officer of Moleculin. “These data point to an unexpected additional benefit. In preclinical models of pancreatic cancer, Annamycin’s antitumor activity appears to depend in part on the immune system. If that observation holds, it broadens both where Annamycin might be useful and how it might be combined.”

Annamycin’s lead clinical program remains the ongoing MIRACLE trial evaluating AnnAraC in patients with relapsed or refractory acute myeloid leukemia (AML), which is the Company’s primary development focus and the basis of its near-term milestones. The pancreatic cancer findings described above are preclinical and are not part of the MIRACLE trial.

About Moleculin Biotech, Inc.

Moleculin Biotech, Inc. is a Phase 2/3 clinical stage pharmaceutical company advancing a pipeline of therapeutic candidates addressing hard-to-treat tumors and viruses. The Company’s lead program, Annamycin (also known as naxtarubicin), is a highly efficacious and well tolerated anthracycline designed to avoid multidrug resistance mechanisms and to lack the cardiotoxicity common with currently prescribed anthracyclines. Annamycin is currently in development for the treatment of relapsed or refractory acute myeloid leukemia (AML) and soft tissue sarcoma (STS) lung metastases.

The Company has begun the MIRACLE (Moleculin R/R AML AnnAraC Clinical Evaluation) Trial (MB-108), a pivotal, adaptive design, multi-center, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 2/3 trial evaluating Annamycin in combination with cytarabine, together referred to as AnnAraC (the combination of Annamycin and cytarabine, also referred to as “Ara-C”) for the treatment of relapsed or refractory acute myeloid leukemia. Following a successful Phase 1B/2 study (MB-106), with input from the FDA, the Company believes it has substantially de-risked the development pathway towards a potential approval for Annamycin for the treatment of AML. This study remains subject to appropriate future filings with potential additional feedback from the FDA and their foreign equivalents.

Additionally, the Company is developing WP1066, an Immune/Transcription Modulator capable of inhibiting p-STAT3 and other oncogenic transcription factors while also stimulating a natural immune response, targeting brain tumors, pancreatic and other cancers. Moleculin also has in its pipeline a portfolio of antimetabolites, including WP1122 for the potential treatment of pathogenic viruses, as well as certain cancer indications.

data.title: How Nvidia Can Benefit From Musk's SpaceX Chip Surprise — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Adam Clark

Nvidia can always count on Elon Musk. The billionaire businessman has just laid out how many artificial-intelligence chips he expects to buy for his SpaceX company's xAI business.

Musk said overnight that the xAI's Memphis data-center complex, called "Colossus," already houses around 780,000 Nvidia AI chips, split across its Hopper and Blackwell generations. The company expects another 220,000 of Nvidia's GB300 Blackwell chips to be operational next week, followed by another 220,000 in October.

"If we get lucky, yet another 220k GB300 by late December," Musk posted on social-media platform X.

Colossus was always set to incorporate a minimum of one million graphics-processing units, according to a statement from the city's chamber of commerce, and Musk previously said SpaceX would exclusively use Nvidia AI chips.

But the latest figures indicate Colossus could house as many as 1.44 million chips before the end of the year, spread across the Colossus 1 and Colossus 2 facilities. The pace of expansion is impressive. And it could help soothe concerns about whether technology companies are overpromising about their abilities to construct data-centers quickly.

For example, Oracle has run into issues with its "Project Jupiter" data-center campus in New Mexico, leading it to deliver a contractual notice to potentially delay payments to its developer, according to The Wall Street Journal. Oracle said in a statement that the project remains on schedule.

Nvidia needs data-center construction to keep pace with its chip sales in order to avoid a glut of hardware sitting in inventories. Musk is doing his part.

Nvidia shares were down 0.4% at $223.61 in early trading Friday.

"Nvidia, of course, is at the epicenter of AI, with an 80% growth rate, and you're paying 22 times forward earnings," said Ken Mahoney, CEO of Mahoney Asset Management. "Typically, Nvidia trades between, let's say, 20 to 40 times forward earnings...It looks actually cheap here."

data.title: Ford F-150 truck production down for nearly a week at Michigan plant, memo says
data.description:
By Nora Eckert

Production of Ford Motor's best-selling F-150 pickup truck has been halted for nearly a week at a Detroit-area plant, according to a memo viewed by Reuters.

All production crews at Dearborn Truck Plant were canceled starting Thursday, through Tuesday, September 29, the memo said. A person familiar with the matter said the outage was because of a supply problem.

Production of F-Series trucks at other plants was also affected. Ford's Kansas City Assembly Plant canceled some shifts this week due to the same issue impacting Dearborn, a person familiar with the matter said. Kentucky Truck Plant near Louisville increased truck production, the person said.

Ford is battling to regain lost output of the trucks after a fire at an aluminum supplier cost it tens of thousands of vehicles of production starting late last year. The automaker's vehicle sales were down about 10% year-over-year through August, with sales of the F-Series down 11%.

The supplier problem that caused the latest disruption was unrelated to the aluminum shortage, the person familiar with the matter said. Reuters was unable to determine the supplier issue at the center of the changes.

Losing even a single day of production is extremely expensive for the automaker, especially for the F-Series, America's best-selling vehicle for 44 years.

General Motors and Ford are projected to have lost more market share in the United States through the first three quarters than any other automakers this year, according to Cox Automotive.

Hyundai and Kia sales combined are expected to surpass Ford in the third quarter, for the first time, Cox said.

data.title: In the U.S.-China Rivalry, One Has a Slight Edge — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Teresa Rivas

President Donald Trump's summit with Chinese leader Xi Jinping puts a spotlight on the precarious U.S.-China relationship and how the two countries are grappling with matters from artificial intelligence to national security. With technology and geopolitics rapidly evolving, it might seem difficult to envision how either of the competing nations might gain the upper hand.

Nonetheless, argues Gavekal Research CEO Louis-Vincent Gave, some clarity can be gained by examining the financial burden each country faces for four essential areas: capital, labor, energy, and government. By Gave's math, most of these have shifted in China's favor, but that doesn't mean investors have to count out the U.S. just yet.

AI remains the biggest question mark-and a double-edged sword.

The cost of capital is likely the easiest to calculate, by looking at short- and longer-term interest rates and each country's respective yield curve. Gave estimates that the cost of capital in the U.S. is currently between 350 basis points and 400 basis points more than in China.

The cost of labor can be somewhat trickier to quantify, as minimum or average wages have to be squared with productivity. Yet China still comes out ahead here, Gave writes, as it has one of the lowest costs of labor in the world-which helps to explain its big annual trade surplus.

The cost of energy is another area where China slightly edges ahead of the U.S. Gave estimates that China has some of the lowest electricity costs in the world for businesses, but the shale revolution dramatically lowered the cost of natural gas and has consequently brought America's energy costs much closer to China's.

"Back in 2011, the U.S. had the cheapest cost of energy, the cheapest cost of capital, very cheap labor (as the U.S. dollar was undervalued following the mortgage bust) and an undervalued currency to boot," Gave writes. "Fast forward to today and China has the lowest cost of capital in the world, a very low cost of electricity, and the lowest cost of labor. And just as with the U.S. dollar in 2011, the renminbi today feels seriously undervalued. So why isn't the Chinese economy growing gangbusters?"

The answer is the fourth and final factor: the cost of government. It's probably the hardest of the four factors to calculate, but for businesses and entrepreneurs, the value of regulation and policy predictability is hard to overstate. One might plausibly argue that the U.S. has struggled with this point during the second Trump Administration, given its trade policies and its speech and actions with regard to Greenland, Venezuela, and Iran, alongside domestic upheaval over a wide range of issues.

However, China scores even lower in this area. Even putting aside the impact of the trade wars with the U.S., its own internal directives have been harmful, from when the "Chinese government pulled the rug from under the feet of a roaring bull market in equities" in 2015 to its directive a few years later mandating domestic banks to stop funding real estate developers, Gave notes.

He also doesn't see much changing in China's favor for a couple of reasons: An improvement in U.S.-China relations seems unlikely and potentially temporary, and consumer-boosting policies are difficult to implement.

As for the U.S., it no longer has many of the tailwinds it enjoyed 15 years ago that best support multiple expansion for U.S. stocks. Instead, the current conditions mean that "a bull market will almost entirely depend on earnings growth rather than multiple expansion," Gave writes.

That's a common opinion, given that the S&P 500 trades near record multiples, and double-digit earnings growth has supported the index as it trades a little more than 1% below its all-time closing high.

Yet Gave closes with a warning that AI remains a wild card. Its failure would mean a higher cost of labor, but its success will cause energy and capital prices to rise. Either scenario could produce the biggest bogeyman for business: policy uncertainty.

Perhaps no AI model can reassure investors that that won't happen.

data.title: 3M Stock Rises on Upgrade. Why This Analyst Likes Its Transformation. — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Al Root

3M stock rose early Friday after catching an upgrade. It isn't an upgrade to Buy, though.

Bernstein analyst Varun Govindaraj upgraded shares to the equivalent of Hold from Sell. His price target went to $171 from $145.

3M stock was up 0.6% in early trading at $168.85, while the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average were up 0.3% and 0.2%, respectively.

"We are upgrading 3M to Market Perform based on a refreshed understanding of the transformation," wrote Govindaraj. "Four factors drive our decision," including an improving economy, margin expansion opportunity, improved R&D spending, and reduced risk tied to 3M's manufacturing of so-called PFAS forever chemicals.

An improving economy is a tailwind for any business. The Institute for Supply Management Purchasing Managers' Index, or ISM PMI, has been above 50, a level that indicates growth, for several months after several years below that level.

Internally, things are improving, too.

CEO Bill Burns took over in May 2024 and has focused on operational efficiency and product innovation. Some green shoots of improvement are emerging.

Comparable sales growth is expected to be 3.5% in 2026, up from 1.5% in 2025 and 1.2% in 2024. As for profit margins, they have increased a couple of percentage points over the past two years. Analysts expect a couple more points of improvement over the next two years.

PFAS liabilities have been an overhang for years, but a roughly $12.5 billion settlement in 2023 gave investors some certainty over the size of potential payments.

Coming into Friday's trading, 3M stock was up about 5% year to date and up 9% over the past 12 months. Shares haven't done much lately, but since Burns took over 3M stock has gained about 70%, 17 percentage points better than the S&P 500.

Overall, Wall Street remains a little skeptical. Only 43% of analysts covering 3M stock rate shares Buy. The average Buy-rating ratio for S&P 500 stocks typically ranges from 55% to 60%.

At least there is one less call to sell the stock.

data.title: Iran will make no nuclear concessions, Iranian official says
data.description:
Key points:
  • Iran says Hormuz to stay shut until US meets all demands
  • Pezeshkian hopes for deal before US elections in November

By Parisa Hafezi and Don Durfee

Iran will show no flexibility over its nuclear program even if the United States accepts its proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, which calls for steps including the lifting of a US naval blockade on Iranian ports, a senior Iranian official told Reuters on Friday.

The official, speaking on condition of anonymity, said the waterway would remain closed until “all of Iran’s conditions are met” by the United States.

Under Iran’s proposal, Tehran has offered to reopen the strategically vital Strait of Hormuz. Within seven days, hostilities would end on all fronts, including Lebanon, the United States would lift its blockade on Iranian ports, release Iran’s frozen funds and waive its oil sanctions, Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi said on Thursday.

The proposal follows a sharp escalation in Middle East tensions after seven months of war between Iran and the United States, with Iran-backed Houthi militias in Yemen launching missiles and drones at Saudi Arabia.

The strait has become the central bargaining chip in efforts to end the US-Iran conflict, with Iran seeking relief from the US blockade that is choking its economy and Washington seeking free passage for ships on the global oil supply route now ‌blocked by Tehran.

In a meeting with journalists on Thursday on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said he hoped a deal with Washington to end the hostilities could be reached before the US midterm elections on November 3.

Tehran said it would be prepared to engage ⁠in detailed negotiations over its nuclear program only after its conditions are met by the US.

But the official said Iran would give no concessions over its rights, including enriching uranium or shipping its highly enriched uranium out of the country, one of the main ​US demands.

Israel, the United States and other Western states have ​long accused Iran of seeking nuclear weapons, including pointing to its move to enrich uranium to 60%, far higher than needed for civilian uses and closer to the 90% needed for a weapon. Iran ​denies seeking nuclear weapons.

The International Atomic Energy Agency estimates that Iran had 440.9 kg of uranium enriched to 60% when Israel and the US attacked Iranian nuclear facilities in June 2025. How much of that ⁠has survived is ​unclear.

Iranian authorities have said that Iran could agree to dilute its most highly enriched uranium.

In May, Reuters reported that Iran's Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei has issued a directive that the country's HEU should not be sent abroad, according to two senior Iranian sources.

data.title: Italy Industry Minister says Volkswagen has no current plans to sell Ducati
data.description:
Italian Industry Minister Adolfo Urso said on Friday that Volkswagen had no plans at the moment to sell its motorbike business Ducati, after meeting with representatives of the German group.

  • Speculation over a potential sale of Ducati rose as Volkswagen, which controls the Italian motorbike maker through its Audi brand, battles the deepest restructuring in its history.

  • Earlier this month, Audi said Ducati was part of a broader review of the automaker's assets, adding no decision had been taken.

  • Urso held a video conference on Friday with Audi CFO Juergen Rittersberger and Ducati CEO Claudio Domenicali to discuss the situation at Ducati, his ministry said in a statement.

  • "Rittersberger reassured participants that Ducati's investment and product plans would continue as planned and confirmed that, at this stage, no decision had been made regarding any changes to Ducati's ownership structure," the ministry said.

data.title: Why First Financial Bancorp (FFBC) Stock Is Up Today
data.description:
What Happened?

Shares of regional banking company First Financial Bancorp jumped 3.4% in the afternoon session after Truist Securities analyst Brian Foran upgraded the stock to Buy from Hold and raised his price target to $37 from $35, as reported by Streetinsider. Foran wrote that he sees mid- to high-single-digit upside to consensus as rising rates filter into results, and that the shares were down more than 10% from their July peak.First Financial is asset-sensitive, so a higher-rate tape feeds net interest income and the estimates built on it. The Buy rating is Foran’s view that the shares can outperform from here. It does not change anything the bank has guided.

After the initial pop, the shares cooled down to $32.61, up 3.4% from the previous close.

What Is The Market Telling Us

First Financial Bancorp’s shares are not very volatile and have only had 3 moves greater than 5% over the last year. In that context, today’s move indicates the market considers this news meaningful, although it might not be something that would fundamentally change its perception of the business.

The biggest move we wrote about over the last year was 11 months ago when the stock dropped 6.4% on the news that disclosures from two lenders raised concerns about deteriorating loan quality across the industry. The drop was triggered by specific incidents that have spooked investors. Zions Bancorp announced a $50 million charge-off—a debt the bank doesn't expect to collect—on a single loan. Separately, Western Alliance Bancorp revealed it was dealing with a borrower who had failed to provide proper collateral. These events are compounding existing anxieties about the regional banking sector, which is already under pressure from elevated interest rates and declining commercial real estate values. The news heightened investor concerns that more cracks could appear in borrowers' creditworthiness, potentially leading to increased loan losses and reduced profitability for other banks in the sector.

First Financial Bancorp is up 30% since the beginning of the year, but at $32.61 per share, it is still trading 9.9% below its 52-week high of $36.18 from July 2026. Investors who bought $1,000 worth of First Financial Bancorp’s shares 5 years ago would now be looking at an investment worth $1,375.
